newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gesamtmetall says could discuss real rise in wages.
newsitem.headline: Gesamtmetall says could discuss real rise in wages.

text.p: German metal and electronics sector employers' federation Gesamtmetall said on Tuesday it would be prepared to discuss a 1997 wage increase of around the rate of inflation.

Responding to the earlier announcement by the IG Metall trade union of its 1997 wage demands, it said that such an increase would however have to be accompanied by measures that would reduce labour costs.
IG Metall earlier set its wage demand for 1997 at an increase of between 4.5 and 5.0 percent.
That range was established using as one basis the expectation of a maximum 2.0 percent rise in consumer prices next year. German inflation is currently around 1.5 percent.

Rejecting the 4.5-5.0 percent range, Gesamtmetall chairman Werner Stumpfe said in a statement: "Wage increases in line with inflation could be discussed -- but only if savings in contractual labour costs also follow," he said.

The two sides are due to start talks on Thursday to resolve a dispute about proposed cuts in sick pay that have sparked mass protests. Employers on Monday withdrew from an immediate implementation of the sick pay cuts in return for promises of industrial peace.
